title: intcomma returns scientific notation for large floats
body: `intcomma()` returns scientific notation for floats of 1e16 and above, without commas. `intcomma(1e15)` is fine but `intcomma(1e16)` returns `'1e+16'` and `intcomma(1.5e20)` returns `'1.5e+20'`. Passing `ndigits=0` avoids it. Cause: float comma formatting follows `repr()`, which switches to exponent notation at 1e16. Small floats too: `intcomma(0.00001)` returns `'1e-05'`.

title: metric() adds a digit when a value rounds into quetta
body: Calling `humanize.metric()` on values just below the quetta threshold (9.996e30, 9.996e31, 9.996e32), and 9999 for comparison. Expected three significant digits like `metric(9999)` → `'10.0 k'`. 9.996e32 has no prefix beyond quetta so it should fall back to scientific notation, e.g. `'1.00 x 10³³'`. Instead output gains an extra digit and the rounding carry stops at exponent 30. macOS, Python 3.14, main branch.

title: Several number functions raise OverflowError on integers larger than a float
body: Most functions in `humanize.number` call `float()` before `int()` to check for NaN/infinity. For integers beyond float range this raises `OverflowError`, which `except (TypeError, ValueError)` does not catch. Affects `apnumber` and `fractional` (raise), `scientific` (raises), and `ordinal`, `intword`, `clamp`, `metric` (show `+Inf` or TypeError in some cases). I plan a PR for `apnumber` and `fractional`; suggest Decimal-based formatting for `scientific`.

title: intword() drops the rounding carry for values >= 10^24 (renders '1000.0 sextillion' instead of '1.0 septillion')
body: `intword(10**24 - 1)` returns `'1000.0 sextillion'` instead of `'1.0 septillion'`; same at 10^27, 10^30, 10^33. Root cause: `if not largest_ordinal and rounded_value * power == powers[ordinal + 1]:` compares a float to an exact int; `float(10**k)` is inexact for k >= 24. Proposed: `rounded_value >= powers[ordinal + 1] // power`. Not overlapping #356.

comments.body: Duplicate of PR #346 (open since 2026-07-06), which fixes the same carry bug with the same diagnosis. Closing in favour of it.

title: precisedelta() silently drops the sign of negative timedeltas
body: `precisedelta(timedelta(seconds=-3661))` and `precisedelta(timedelta(seconds=3661))` both give `'1 hour, 1 minute and 1 second'`. Tested humanize 4.16.0 and master on Python 3.13; docstring and tests don't cover negative input. Options: keep the sign with a leading minus like `str(timedelta)`, or raise / document non-negative only. Happy to send a PR.

title: `naturalsize()` raises `ValueError` for custom format strings with text
body: `naturalsize(1500, format='Size: %.1f')` worked in 4.15.0 but raises `ValueError: could not convert string to float: 'Size: 1.5'` in 4.16.0 and main. Caused by #329 (unit rollover), which passes the whole formatted string to `float()`. Fix: only roll over when the result is purely numeric, or compute the rounded mantissa separately. Please add a regression test with a prefix and a suffix. Found via differential testing.

title: intword: values between 10^36 and a googol format as huge decillion counts, and rounding to the next unit does not carry
body: `intword` formats values between 10^36 and a googol (10^100) as enormous decillion counts: `intword(10**50)` is a 17-digit decillion count, and a value just below a googol never carries to `'1.0 googol'`. Similar to the `metric()` boundary bug fixed in #328. Options: fall back to `str(value)` in that range, or carry correctly and fall back when no larger unit fits. I can write regression tests once you pick a behaviour.

comments.body: Sorry, cleaning up my issues. It should stay open; PR #364 addresses it. Reopening; happy to add the boundary tests to that PR.

title: Percentages and ratios
body: If I'm not mistaken there is no feature yet to humanize a ratio (between 0 and 1) or a percentage (between 0-100). It can be just one function to handle both, with two possible inputs (ratio= or percent=), returning a truncated percent string, optionally with a decimal comma like `12,5%`, precision customizable in number of decimals like `precisedelta`.

title: Proposal for adding more 'intword' words
body: I made an idle game with huge numbers and humanize stops humanizing after decillion. I added words for larger powers to number.py, from undecillion (10^36) up to googol (10^100), e.g. `NS_("undecillion", "undecillion")`, `NS_("googol", "googol")`. Used ChatGPT for the longer names. Can this go in a new version?

title: Proposal for additional `conjunction` parameter in `natural_list` function
body: Proposal: a parameter to choose 'and' or 'or' in `natural_list`. Originally a boolean `conjunction=True` ('and') / `False` ('or'): `natural_list([1, 2, 3])` → `'1, 2 and 3'`, `natural_list([1, 2, 3], conjunction=False)` → `'1, 2 or 3'`. i18n could be a separate issue. Is `conjunction` the best name?

comments.body: More general: let `conjunction` take any string, like 'or' or 'and also'. Name is open to change.
Any-string is interesting but worries me for i18n. I still prefer `conjunction` over connector/joiner. I'll open a separate issue about empty lists.
natural_list has no i18n yet, so handle that separately. Later we can pre-bake 'and'/'or' and custom text can use gettext.
